jsonLd.name: Sculptra (Collagen Stimulation)
jsonLd.description: Sculptra is an injectable biostimulator made of poly-L-lactic acid that gradually rebuilds the patient's own collagen, restoring facial structural volume over a course of two to three sessions, four to six weeks apart, with results that may last up to two years.
jsonLd.bodyLocation: Face — temples, mid-face, cheeks, jawline, lower face
jsonLd.preparation: Avoid blood-thinning medications, alcohol, and intense physical activity for 48 hours before the session. Arrive with clean skin, free of make-up. Inform the medical team of any active infection, recent dental work, or autoimmune flare.
jsonLd.followup: Massage the treated area five minutes, five times a day, for five days. Avoid sun exposure, sauna, and intense exercise for 48 hours. Sleep slightly elevated the first night. Attend the follow-up appointment four to six weeks after the session.
jsonLd.howPerformed: After medical assessment, the area is cleansed and topical anaesthetic applied. Reconstituted Sculptra is injected with cannula or needle into deep dermal or supraperiosteal planes following a personalised plan. The session ends with manual massage to distribute the product evenly.

mainEntity.name: How many Sculptra sessions will I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients complete a protocol of two to three sessions spaced four to six weeks apart. The exact number depends on the degree of volume loss, your collagen response, and the aesthetic goal defined during your consultation in Miami. Some patients with mild changes need only two sessions; others with more pronounced volume loss benefit from a third visit to refine the result.

The visible change builds gradually as new collagen is produced. Most patients begin to notice firmer, more rested-looking skin around four to six weeks after the first session. The complete result matures roughly three months after the final session of the protocol, which is why patience and adherence to the plan matter so much with Sculptra.

mainEntity.name: How long do Sculptra results last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete Sculptra protocol may last up to two years, depending on age, lifestyle, sun exposure, and overall skin quality. Because the product stimulates your own collagen, the duration tends to exceed that of standard hyaluronic acid fillers. Many patients schedule a maintenance session once a year to preserve volume and structure over time.

Discomfort is generally mild. We apply topical anaesthetic before treatment and the diluent contains lidocaine, which numbs the area as the product is delivered. Most patients describe the sensation as pressure rather than sharp pain. Cannula technique, when appropriate, further reduces discomfort and the chance of bruising during the session.

mainEntity.name: How is Sculptra different from hyaluronic acid fillers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hyaluronic acid fillers add volume the moment they are placed and are reversible with hyaluronidase. Sculptra is a biostimulator: it does not fill instantly; it triggers your own dermis to produce collagen over weeks. The result is a slower, more structural change with longer duration. They are complementary tools used inside a personalised plan, not direct substitutes.

mainEntity.name: Is the post-treatment massage really necessary?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The five-five-five massage — five minutes, five times a day, for five days — helps distribute the product evenly and reduces the chance of palpable nodules. We will demonstrate the technique at the end of your session and provide written instructions. Patients who follow the protocol consistently tend to obtain smoother and more predictable outcomes.

mainEntity.name: Can Sculptra be combined with other treatments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Sculptra integrates well with neuromodulators, hyaluronic acid fillers for fine detail, energy-based devices, and skin-quality protocols such as PRP or mesotherapy. Sequencing matters: we typically address structural volume first with Sculptra, then refine surface texture and dynamic lines. Ronal Perdomo, APRN, FNP-C will design the order and timing during your consultation.

Sculptra is not advisable during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in patients with active skin infections in the treatment area, a history of keloid scarring, active autoimmune flares, or known hypersensitivity to any component of the product. A complete medical history is reviewed before every treatment to confirm suitability and to design the safest plan.

hero.title: Sculptra in Miami: Collagen Stimulation for Natural Volume
hero.lede: Sculptra is an injectable biostimulator made of poly-L-lactic acid that gradually rebuilds your own collagen, restoring facial structure and volume over a course of two to three sessions.

blocks.title: What it does for you
list: Stimulates the patient's own collagen instead of relying solely on external filler material.
Restores structural volume in the temples, mid-face, jawline, and lower face with a natural look.
Refines skin quality, density, and tone in the treated areas as collagen rebuilds.
Produces gradual, discreet change that friends and colleagues notice slowly.
Offers long-lasting results that may persist up to two years with proper maintenance.
Treats global facial ageing rather than a single line or fold.
Pairs well with neuromodulators, hyaluronic acid fillers, and energy-based treatments inside a personalised plan.
